**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.4.8](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.4.8).

This is the first build of the 0.5.0 line, and the first XEarthLayer release with a **macOS** build. It comes with a rebuilt scenery library: every region has been regenerated from scratch, under new region codes, and is published on a separate staging library rather than the one your current install uses. Please follow the setup below in order, because the old and new scenery overlap and should not be installed side by side.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.1-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` tarballs are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

---

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-alpha.1
```

**macOS:** install [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io) first, including the one-time approval of its system extension. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/macos.md) walks through it.

Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you. With Safari:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.1-arm64-macos
```

With any other browser:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-alpha.1-arm64-macos.tar.gz
```

Then:

```bash
xattr -c xearthlayer         # the binary is unsigned: clear the download quarantine
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-alpha.1
```

The binary is not signed, so without the `xattr` step macOS refuses to run it, showing **"xearthlayer" Not Opened: Apple could not verify "xearthlayer" is free of malware**. If you see that, click **Done**, not Move to Trash, and run the `xattr` line. If `xearthlayer` is not found, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to your shell profile and open a new terminal.

New to XEarthLayer on this machine? Run `xearthlayer setup` after installing the binary, then continue from step 4.

### 2. Let it move your configuration

XEarthLayer no longer keeps everything in `~/.xearthlayer`. The first command you run copies your `config.ini` to the platform's standard location (`~/.config/xearthlayer/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/XEarthLayer/` on macOS) and may ask you to confirm. Accepting is safe: nothing else is moved, and your existing scenery, cache and packages stay where they are. The old `config.ini` is kept, so v0.4.8 still works if you go back to it.

Then bring the configuration up to date. This adds the new settings with their defaults and removes ones that no longer do anything:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

### 3. Remove every existing XEarthLayer scenery package

The rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the two must not be installed together. **Do this before installing anything new**, because the commands below select packages by the start of their region code, and the new codes start the same way as the old ones.

```bash
xearthlayer packages list
```

Then remove the old ortho and overlay packages. This loop covers every old region. For a region you never installed it prints `Error: Package manager error: No package matches 'as'`, which is harmless and just means there was nothing to remove:

```bash
for r in af as eu na oc sa; do
  xearthlayer packages remove $r --force
  xearthlayer packages remove $r --type overlay --force
done
xearthlayer packages list    # should report no packages installed
```

There is nothing to clean up by hand in `Custom Scenery`: XEarthLayer rebuilds its entries there from the installed packages every time it starts.

### 4. Point XEarthLayer at the staging library

```bash
xearthlayer config set packages.library_url https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samsoir/xearthlayer-regional-scenery/staging/xearthlayer_package_library.txt
```

To go back to the stable library later, set it to `https://xearthlayer.app/packages/xearthlayer_package_library.txt`.

Have each ortho package bring its overlay with it, so you test the full set:

```bash
xearthlayer config set packages.auto_install_overlays true
```

### 5. Install the regions you fly

A region code, or the start of one, installs every package beneath it, each with its overlay: `xearthlayer packages install na` installs all of North America, `xearthlayer packages install eu-west` just western Europe.

| Region | Covers | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `NA-USA-BERMUDA-BAHAMAS` | Contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii, Bermuda, the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos | 14.1 GB |
| `NA-MEXICO-CENTRAL` | Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean | 4.5 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-WEST` | Canada west of 95° W | 10.2 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-EAST` | Canada east of 95° W | 13.2 GB |
| `NA-GREENLAND` | Greenland | 0.8 GB |
| `SA-WEST` | Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the Guianas | 9.2 GB |
| `SA-EAST` | Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, the Falklands | 8.8 GB |
| `EU-WEST` | Europe west of Russia, Iceland, Scandinavia, the Mediterranean | 16.1 GB |
| `EU-EAST` | European Russia west of the Urals | 3.7 GB |
| `AF-NORTH` | North and West Africa | 7.3 GB |
| `AF-SOUTH` | Central, East and Southern Africa | 9.1 GB |
| `AS-INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-HIMALAYAN` | Middle East, Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent | 16.8 GB |
| `AS-CHINA-MONGOLIA` | China and Mongolia | 18.5 GB |
| `AS-ASIA-PACIFIC` | Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, the Philippines | 11.6 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-CENTRAL` | Siberia from the Urals to Lake Baikal | 4.8 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-EAST` | The Russian Far East | 6.4 GB |
| `OC-AUSTRALIA-NZ-PACIFIC` | Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands | 5.5 GB |

Sizes are download sizes; installed size is about the same. The whole world is about 161 GB. Antarctica is not available yet. Installing several regions at once is faster than one at a time: each package installs while the next one downloads.

### 6. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What we most want tested

### 1. X-Plane never waits behind prefetch

Prefetch used to share a queue with X-Plane's own tile requests, so at a boundary crossing or a turn, a tile X-Plane needed could sit behind thousands of prefetch jobs until the generation timeout. Prefetch now runs in its own lane and stands aside completely while X-Plane is waiting on a tile.

**What to look for:** stutters or pauses at DSF boundary crossings and in turns, and purple or placeholder tiles. The dashboard's Scenery System pane shows how long X-Plane waited for tiles over the session (`p50`, `p95`, `max`) and counts any timeouts. A long flight with zero timeouts is a useful report too.

### 2. Night lighting

Cities on ortho scenery used to go dark at night wherever X-Plane's autogen lights did not reach. XEarthLayer now generates the lit textures X-Plane asks for at night, from the night recipe in each package and the lit art in your own X-Plane installation. It is on by default.

**What to look for:** a night flight over a city you know. Lighting that sits where it should, brightness that looks right, and no visible tile edges or repeating pattern. The dashboard's Status pane shows whether night lighting is active; "X-Plane was not found" there means XEarthLayer could not locate your X-Plane installation's lit art.

### 3. The new scenery

Every region has been rebuilt with new mesh, water and overlays. **What to look for:** missing tiles over land, seams between regions, water in the wrong place, and overlay roads or buildings that do not sit on the ortho.

### 4. macOS

This is the first macOS build. Anything that differs from what Linux users describe is worth a report, starting with installation.

### 5. SimHeaven X-World Pro

If you use X-World Pro, set `xearthlayer config set packages.xworld_pro true`. XEarthLayer then detects which continents X-World Pro covers, leaves its own overlays out there, and checks your `scenery_packs.ini` order at startup.

### The dashboard

There is a new Status pane at the bottom: X-Plane's frame rate, whether GPU encoding, night lighting and X-World Pro are active. If prefetch costs you frame rate, `prefetch.capacity_share` (default 0.35, range 0.05 to 0.50) sets how much of the machine prefetch may use.

## How to report

Find your log with:

```bash
xearthlayer config get logging.file
```

It is no longer in `~/.xearthlayer`. By default it is `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/xearthlayer.log` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS.

> **Copy the log before you launch again. It is overwritten on every start.**

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the log, and what looked wrong. If something did look wrong, the whole log is better. Please include the output of:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**The macOS binary is unsigned.** It needs the `xattr -c` step above. Signing comes before the stable release.

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**

**Chunk download 404s from the imagery provider.** Some tiles genuinely do not exist at the requested zoom. They are no longer retried, and the affected tiles are served but not cached.
